headline: Norway's Electric Car Revolution Hits 98.7% in August
meta_description: Electric vehicles now dominate Norway's new car market, with EVs making up 98.7% of registrations in August and 97.8% so far in 2026.
summary_short: Norway's electric vehicle adoption has reached near-total completion, with EVs accounting for record-breaking shares of new car sales this year.
body:
Electric vehicles made up 98.7% of new passenger car registrations in Norway during August, marking a decisive moment in the country's automotive transformation. The milestone reflects years of sustained momentum toward a fully electrified fleet.

Through 2026 so far, electric cars account for 97.8% of all new passenger vehicles sold in Norway—a figure that underscores how thoroughly the transition has reshaped the market. What once seemed like a distant goal has become the unmistakable reality of Norwegian roads, where buying an electric car is now the overwhelming norm rather than the exception.

The achievement speaks to the power of consistent policy, infrastructure investment, and market forces working in alignment. For a nation that once depended heavily on oil exports, the shift represents not just environmental progress but a fundamental reimagining of what transportation means.
quick_facts: 98.7% of new cars registered in Norway in August were electric
97.8% of new passenger vehicles sold in Norway through 2026 are EVs
Electric vehicles now dominate Norway's automotive market completely
